name: The Huntoon Place, Harrison and Clinton Streets

function.note: 'The house was occupied for many years by Charles Huntoon, who died there some years before its destruction' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717).

built.note: 'Built by Judge J. D. Caton, nearly half a century before' its destruction (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717); the year is reconstructed from that.

research_note: THE HUNTOON PLACE, built by T-3831 for the 1871 scene: 'The northwest quarter of this large block of ground was known as the "Huntoon Place," having the appearance of a large country farm-house. The residence stood well back from the street, and the lot was filled with large trees. The house was a landmark, having been built by Judge J. D. Caton, nearly half a century before. The quaint old mansion had twelve stacks of chimneys ... a picturesque place in a neighborhood of puffing and impertinent modern factories' (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717). No picture of it is known.

documented_range.note: Standing from Judge Caton's day until the fire destroyed it (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717).

position.symbolic_location: The south-east corner of Harrison and Clinton Streets, set well back in its grounds.
position.note: The north-west quarter of the block (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717), the house well back from both streets; its place in the grounds is reconstructed. The footprint's origin is local E -246.0 N -1452.0.

derivation.reason: Laid out from the accounts' description of the block against the 1871 plan's streets; no traced frontage for the 1871 city is in data/traces/street_control.json to recompute it from.

footprint.note: The north-west quarter of the block bounded by Harrison, Mather, Canal and Clinton (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717): the house's grounds.

fire.note: The block bounded by Harrison, Mather, Canal and Clinton burned (Andreas vol. 2, p. 717).
